patients.label: 53-year-old man with treatment-resistant schizophrenia / schizoaffective disorder bipolar type receiving dual long-acting injectable antipsychotics

identity_evidence.quote: A 53-year-old male with a past psychiatric history of schizoaffective disorder bipolar type

attribution_limitations: Quetiapine timeline conflict: narrative says he requested quetiapine on day 20 and was briefly adherent for 5 days before consistently refusing, but the Table shows quetiapine taken only on day 20 (50 mg), refused days 21-29, then taken days 30-34 (200 mg on days 30-33, 400 mg on day 34), refused days 35-38 and discontinued day 39.
Diagnosis is given as both schizoaffective disorder bipolar type (past history) and treatment-resistant schizophrenia (case title/abstract); both retained.

Clozapine start date is uncertain ("exact start date is difficult to determine") and the abstract says he failed oral clozapine, while the Table shows refusal rather than documented pharmacologic failure; no clozapine concentrations were obtained.
Discharge is not documented; oral haloperidol was started on day 48 to facilitate discharge and the last Table day is 55.

Improvement after the second LAI is attributed by the authors to dual LAI therapy, but concurrent oral haloperidol and ongoing paliperidone palmitate are also documented; the report is a single uncontrolled case.
Haloperidol "up to 15 mg ... during this inpatient admission" cannot be a cumulative total: Table emergency haloperidol before day 40 exceeds 15 mg; it equals the day-4 amount (5 IM × 3).

Text says aggression resolution was "exemplified by the lack of emergency medications administered after dual LAI", but the next sentences report 1 emergency antipsychotic over 2 weeks and the Table shows an emergency haloperidol 5 mg IM dose on day 47.
